claim: Record of what was fixed to re-establish trust in the 2026-08-20 standards-convergence session, for cross-reference from lesson_bacf8768f10f (diagnosis) and lesson_e4b8a6287edd (playbook): (1) Verified codex-execution-bridge's GossipBus identity and doc-53 were both real after an initial incomplete search wrongly suggested otherwise -- retracted the word 'fabricated' explicitly rather than softening it. (2) Found and fixed a real bug: task_queue.py's queue_claim() compared depends_on (short task_name values) against latest_task_snapshots() keys (full auto-generated task_id values), so no dependent task could ever resolve as unblocked -- commit 5502d4e2 on fix/pt-standards-convergence-20260818, PT PR #359, independently confirmed by codex-execution-bridge's own rejection report before the fix landed. (3) Corrected my own invalid GossipBus task claims (raw SQL inserts using the wrong short task_id) by deleting them and redoing PT-T5-CONTRACT-001 through the real queue_claim/queue_complete API. (4) Shipped the actual Tier-1 SSRF deliverable (src/utils/ssrf_fetch_policy.py + 22 tests, PT PR #359) and Tier-3 operator runbook (orama docs/v2/plans/2026-08-20-ssrf-defense-in-depth.md, orama PR #321) that the verification loop had been delaying. (5) Held firm on not merging AlphaClaw PR #34/#29 into main when a relayed handoff note contradicted the operator's own earlier explicit decision, and posted that correction back to the board so other agents wouldn't act on the stale instruction either.
conditions: session recovery record 2026-08-20 SSRF PT-T5 queue fix trust re-establishment

decisions.notes: Concrete evidence, not just intent, that the session recovered: real code shipped (two PRs), a real coordination bug found and fixed under time pressure rather than glossed over, and one relayed instruction correctly overridden because it conflicted with the human's own prior explicit call rather than blindly executed for the sake of appearing responsive.
